translation: For any closed arithmetic sentence σ, Def2(σ) means that σ is true in the standard model of the natural numbers. For any set K of arithmetic sentences, Def3(K) means that for every arithmetic sentence σ, if σ belongs to K, then Def2(σ) holds. It does not require K to contain every true sentence. For any such K, Def4(K) means that no contradiction is derivable in classical first-order logic using K itself as the axiom set. Def4 does not require Def3(K). None of the definitions requires K to be recursively enumerable or closed under deduction.

divergences.description: Def2 specializes the passage’s informal truth set T to closed arithmetic sentences true in the standard natural numbers. It defines a predicate rather than naming a set; the corresponding set is {σ | Def2 σ}.
K is a set parameter. Nothing in the target identifies which sentences are “absolutely provable” or producible by the idealized human mind; that interpretation of K must be supplied externally.
The quoted passage identifies T and K but does not explicitly state K ⊆ T. Def3 supplies that inclusion as the definition of soundness, not as an assertion that the intended K satisfies it.

Def4 treats any K as an axiom set and defines its consistency externally as nonderivability of contradiction. Instantiating it with PA captures the passage’s assumption that PA is consistent, but Def4 is not the arithmetic sentence Con(PA) that expresses that assumption inside arithmetic.

judgement.summary: The target faithfully defines the three notions at the metalevel. It neither establishes soundness for the intended K nor states either of the quoted incompleteness theorems.
